Pack tightly into a casing (or baking dish) and steam for 2-3 hours until firm.

dishes.name: Bangers and Mash
dishes.description: British comfort food pairing sausages with mashed potato and gravy.
steps: Boil potatoes until very tender, then drain.
Mash the potatoes with butter and warm milk until smooth.
Grill or pan-fry the sausages until browned and cooked through.
Warm the onion gravy.
Serve the sausages over mashed potato, topped generously with gravy.

dishes.name: Stroopwafel
dishes.description: Thin waffle cookies sandwiched with a caramel filling.
steps: Make a rich, slightly sweet yeasted dough and let it rest.
Divide into small balls and press each in a hot waffle iron until thin and golden.
While still warm, slice each waffle in half horizontally.
Spread caramel syrup filling on the cut side of one half.
Sandwich with the other half, pressing gently to seal.

dishes.name: Moules Frites
dishes.description: Steamed mussels served with a side of crispy fries, Belgium's signature dish.
steps: Sauté shallot in butter until soft.
Add white wine and bring to a simmer.
Add cleaned mussels, cover, and steam until they open, about 5-7 minutes, discarding any that stay closed.
Fry potatoes until golden and crisp.
Serve the mussels in their broth alongside a big portion of fries.

dishes.name: Bitterballen
dishes.description: Deep-fried Dutch meat croquettes, a popular bar snack.
steps: Make a very thick, well-seasoned beef ragout, then chill it until firm.
Shape the cold ragout into small balls.
Dredge each ball in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Deep fry until deeply golden and crisp.
Serve hot with mustard for dipping.

dishes.name: Cheese Fondue
dishes.description: Melted cheese shared communally, eaten by dipping bread on long forks.
steps: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with a cut garlic clove.
Heat white wine gently, then gradually melt in grated gruyere and emmental, stirring constantly.
Toss the cheese with a little cornstarch first to help it stay smooth.
Keep the pot warm over a low flame at the table.
Dip cubes of bread on long forks, swirling to keep the cheese moving.

dishes.name: Raclette
dishes.description: Melted cheese scraped over potatoes and accompaniments, both a dish and a social meal.
steps: Boil small potatoes until tender.
Slice raclette cheese and melt it under a broiler or in a raclette grill.
Pour the melted cheese over the warm potatoes.
Serve with cured meats, cornichons, and pickled onions on the side.
Repeat with fresh cheese and potatoes throughout the meal, as raclette is eaten in rounds.

dishes.name: Sachertorte
dishes.description: Dense Viennese chocolate cake with a thin layer of apricot jam.
steps: Bake a dense chocolate sponge cake.
Slice the cake in half and spread a thin layer of apricot jam in the middle.
Reassemble and coat the whole cake with more apricot jam.
Pour a glossy chocolate glaze over the top, letting it drip down the sides.
Let the glaze set before slicing and serving, traditionally with whipped cream.

dishes.name: Gyro
dishes.description: Greek wrapped sandwich of spiced meat, similar in spirit to shawarma and doner.
steps: Marinate meat (or stack pre-seasoned meat) and roast on a vertical spit, or pan-sear thin slices.
Slice off crispy edges as they form.
Warm pita bread.
Spread tzatziki on the pita.
Fill with meat, tomato, onion, and more tzatziki, then wrap.

dishes.name: Greek Salad
dishes.description: Simple salad of tomato, cucumber, olives, and feta, no lettuce involved.
steps: Chop tomato, cucumber, and green pepper into large chunks.
Combine with red onion and Kalamata olives in a bowl.
Top with a thick slab of feta cheese.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and a little dried oregano.
Serve without dressing on the vegetables themselves, letting the olive oil do the work.

dishes.name: Ćevapi
dishes.description: Grilled minced meat fingers popular across the former Yugoslavia.
steps: Mix ground meats with garlic, baking soda, and salt, kneading well to develop a springy texture.
Rest the mixture in the fridge for a few hours or overnight.
Shape into small finger-sized sausages.
Grill over high heat, turning often, until charred outside and cooked through.
Serve in warm flatbread with chopped onion.

dishes.name: Burek
dishes.description: Flaky spiral or layered pastry filled with meat, cheese, or spinach.
steps: Cook ground beef with minced onion until browned, then let it cool.
Layer sheets of phyllo, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread a portion of the meat filling and roll into a coil, or layer flat depending on style.
Coil the filled rolls into a spiral in a round pan, or cut into portions.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until deeply golden and crisp, about 35-40 minutes.

dishes.name: Sarmale
dishes.description: Romanian cabbage rolls stuffed with spiced meat and rice.
steps: Mix ground pork with rice, minced onion, and seasoning.
Place a spoonful of filling on each blanched cabbage leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Layer the rolls snugly in a large pot.
Cover with tomato sauce and enough water to just cover.
Simmer gently for 1.5-2 hours until the rice is cooked and the rolls are tender.

dishes.name: Goulash
dishes.description: Hungarian paprika-spiced beef and vegetable stew.
steps: Sauté onion until deeply softened.
Add paprika and stir briefly (careful not to burn it).
Add beef and brown lightly, then add enough water or stock to cover.
Simmer covered for 1.5 hours until the beef is nearly tender, then add potato and caraway.
Continue simmering until the potato is tender and the stew has thickened.

dishes.name: Lángos
dishes.description: Deep-fried Hungarian flatbread, often topped with sour cream and cheese.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, and mashed potato with warm water into a soft dough, then let rise about an hour.
Stretch portions of dough into flat rounds.
Deep fry each round in hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides.
Rub the hot langos with a cut garlic clove.
Top with sour cream and shredded cheese if desired.

dishes.name: Trdelník
dishes.description: Spit-rolled pastry dough coated in cinnamon sugar, popular street food.
steps: Make a sweet yeasted dough with flour, milk, sugar, and yeast, then let it rise.
Roll into long ropes and wrap each around a wooden spit or rolling pin.
Roll the wrapped dough in sugar and cinnamon.
Grill or bake over rotating heat until golden and crisp outside.
Slide off the spit and serve warm.

dishes.name: Kielbasa
dishes.description: Smoked Polish sausage eaten on its own or in stews.
steps: Mix ground and finely cubed pork with garlic, marjoram, and seasoning.
Stuff the mixture into casings, twisting into links.
Smoke or simmer the sausages until cooked through.
Finish by grilling or pan-searing until the skin is browned and crisp.
Serve with mustard and rye bread.

dishes.name: Smørrebrød
dishes.description: Open-faced Danish sandwich, artfully topped with fish, meat, or cheese.
steps: Spread a thin, even layer of butter on each slice of rye bread.
Arrange a chosen topping (smoked fish, roast beef, or egg) neatly over the bread.
Add complementary garnishes like dill, pickles, or radish slices.
Keep the toppings visually arranged rather than piled.
Serve open-faced, eaten with a knife and fork.

dishes.name: Köttbullar
dishes.description: Swedish meatballs served with a creamy sauce and tart lingonberry jam.
steps: Soak breadcrumbs in cream until softened.
Mix with ground meat, egg, and grated onion, then form into small round meatballs.
Fry the meatballs in butter until browned all over and cooked through.
Make a pan sauce with the drippings, cream, and a little stock.
Serve the meatballs with the sauce and lingonberry jam on the side.

dishes.name: Gravlax
dishes.description: Cured raw salmon flavored with dill, salt, and sugar.
steps: Mix salt and sugar together.
Rub the mixture generously over both sides of the salmon.
Pack fresh dill on top of the fish.
Wrap tightly and refrigerate under a weight for 48-72 hours, turning occasionally.
Scrape off the cure, slice thinly on an angle, and serve with mustard sauce.

dishes.name: Lutefisk
dishes.description: Traditional Norwegian dish of whitefish preserved and rehydrated with lye.
steps: Soak the dried fish in plain water for several days, changing the water daily, to soften it.
Soak the fish in a lye solution for a few days until it becomes gelatinous.
Soak again in fresh water for several more days to remove the lye completely.
Poach or bake the prepared fish gently until just cooked through.
Serve with melted butter, boiled potatoes, and peas.

dishes.name: Shakshuka
dishes.description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
steps: Sauté onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add crushed tomato and cumin, simmering until it thickens into a rich sauce, about 15 minutes.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks remain runny.
Serve directly from the pan with crusty bread.

dishes.name: Sabich
dishes.description: Israeli pita sandwich built around fried eggplant and egg.
steps: Fry sliced eggplant until deeply golden and soft.
Warm the pita bread.
Spread tahini sauce inside the pita.
Layer in fried eggplant and sliced hard-boiled egg.
Drizzle with amba sauce and add pickled vegetables before serving.

dishes.name: Maqluba
dishes.description: Layered rice and meat dish flipped upside down for serving, its name means 'upside-down'.
steps: Fry eggplant and cauliflower slices until golden, then set aside.
Brown chicken pieces with mixed spices in the bottom of a large pot.
Layer the fried vegetables over the chicken, then top with rice.
Add stock to just cover, then cook covered on low heat until the rice is tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Invert the whole pot onto a large platter to reveal the layered dish.

dishes.name: Mansaf
dishes.description: Jordan's national dish: lamb cooked in a tangy fermented yogurt sauce over rice.
steps: Simmer lamb in water until tender, about 1.5 hours, reserving the broth.
Dissolve jameed in some of the lamb broth, whisking until smooth.
Simmer the lamb in the jameed sauce until well coated and the sauce is creamy.
Cook rice separately and spread over a bed of flatbread on a large platter.
Top with the lamb and jameed sauce, and scatter toasted almonds over the top.

dishes.name: Kibbeh
dishes.description: Torpedo-shaped fried croquettes of bulgur and spiced minced meat.
steps: Soak bulgur in water until softened, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Blend or knead the bulgur with half the ground lamb and spices to form a smooth outer shell mixture.
Cook the remaining lamb with onion and pine nuts for the filling.
Shape the bulgur mixture into a shell around a spoonful of filling, forming a torpedo shape.
Deep fry until deeply golden and crisp.

dishes.name: Kabsa
dishes.description: Saudi Arabia's spiced rice and meat dish, similar to biryani.
steps: Brown chicken or lamb pieces with kabsa spice blend.
Sauté onion, garlic, and tomato in the same pot.
Add rice and stock, stirring to combine.
Nestle the meat back into the pot, cover, and cook until the rice is tender.
Fluff and serve topped with toasted nuts and raisins.

dishes.name: Mandi
dishes.description: Yemeni rice and meat dish traditionally slow-cooked in an underground pit.
steps: Rub the meat generously with mandi spice blend and let it marinate.
Slow-cook or smoke the meat until very tender, traditionally in an underground pit or tandoor.
Cook rice with saffron and some of the meat drippings for flavor and color.
Shred or portion the cooked meat.
Serve the meat over the fragrant rice.

dishes.name: Machboos
dishes.description: Spiced rice dish common across the Gulf, similar to biryani and kabsa.
steps: Brown the meat with onion and baharat spice blend.
Add dried lime and enough water to cover, then simmer until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat and cook rice in the same spiced broth.
Return the meat to the pot or layer it over the rice.
Serve hot with a side salad or yogurt sauce.

dishes.name: İskender Kebab
dishes.description: Sliced doner meat over pita, topped with tomato sauce, butter, and yogurt.
steps: Layer cubed pita bread in the bottom of a serving dish.
Arrange thin slices of doner-style meat over the bread.
Pour warm tomato sauce over the meat.
Add a generous dollop of yogurt to the side.
Finish with a drizzle of sizzling melted butter just before serving.

dishes.name: Pide
dishes.description: Turkish flatbread shaped like a boat, topped and baked until crisp.
steps: Roll dough into an oval and pinch up the edges to form a boat shape.
Fill the center with cheese or a spiced meat mixture.
Crack an egg over the top if using the cheese-and-egg style.
Bake at high heat until the crust is golden and crisp.
Serve hot, sliced into strips.

dishes.name: Muhammara
dishes.description: Spicy-sweet Syrian dip of roasted peppers and walnuts.
steps: Roast red peppers until charred, then peel and seed them.
Blend the peppers with walnuts, breadcrumbs, pomegranate molasses, and cumin.
Blend until mostly smooth but with a little texture remaining.
Taste and adjust the tartness with more molasses if needed.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve with flatbread.

dishes.name: Brik
dishes.description: Tunisian fried pastry filled with egg, tuna, and spices, eaten by biting carefully.

ingredients.name: thin pastry (malsouka or spring roll wrapper)

ingredient_names: thin pastry (malsouka or spring roll wrapper)
steps: Lay a sheet of thin pastry and place flaked tuna, capers, and parsley in the center.
Crack a raw egg on top of the filling.
Fold the pastry over into a half-moon, sealing the edges carefully so the egg doesn't leak.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp, being careful when flipping.
Serve immediately while the egg is still soft inside.

dishes.name: Lablabi
dishes.description: Tunisian chickpea soup poured over torn bread and topped with harissa.
steps: Warm the cooked chickpeas in their broth with cumin.
Place torn stale bread in serving bowls.
Ladle the hot chickpeas and broth over the bread to soften it.
Top each bowl with a poached egg and a spoonful of harissa.
Drizzle with olive oil before serving.

dishes.name: Chakchouka
dishes.description: North African cousin of shakshuka, eggs poached in spiced vegetables.
steps: Sauté bell pepper and garlic until softened.
Add chopped tomato and harissa, simmering until it thickens into a rich sauce.
Make wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but yolks remain soft.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

dishes.name: Mechoui
dishes.description: Whole lamb slow-roasted until falling off the bone, served at celebrations.
steps: Rub the whole lamb generously with salt, cumin, and melted butter.
Skewer the lamb on a spit for roasting, or place in a very low oven.
Roast slowly over low heat for several hours, basting occasionally, until the meat is completely tender and falls off the bone.
Baste with more butter throughout cooking for a crisp exterior.
Carve and serve with extra cumin and salt on the side for dipping.

dishes.name: Om Ali
dishes.description: Egyptian bread pudding baked with milk, nuts, and raisins.
steps: Bake puff pastry until golden and crisp, then break into pieces.
Layer the pastry pieces in a baking dish with mixed nuts and raisins.
Heat milk with sugar until warm and slightly thickened.
Pour the sweetened milk over the pastry and nuts.
Top with cream and bake or broil until golden and bubbling on top.

dishes.name: Thieboudienne
dishes.description: Senegal's national dish of fish and rice cooked in a rich tomato sauce.
steps: Stuff fish with a paste of herbs and pepper, then sear until browned.
Sauté onion and tomato paste, then add water to make a broth.
Add the fish and mixed vegetables, simmering until everything is tender; remove and set aside.
Cook rice in the remaining flavorful broth until tender.
Serve the rice topped with the fish and vegetables.

dishes.name: Yassa
dishes.description: Tangy Senegalese dish of marinated chicken or fish with caramelized onions.
steps: Marinate chicken in lemon juice, mustard, and sliced onion for at least 2 hours.
Grill or sear the chicken until browned, then set aside.
Cook the marinated onions down slowly until soft and caramelized.
Return the chicken to the pan with the onions and bay leaves, adding a little water.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened, then serve over rice.

dishes.name: Fufu
dishes.description: Starchy, stretchy dough pounded from cassava or plantain, eaten with soups and stews.
steps: Peel and boil cassava or plantain until very soft.
Drain well.
Pound the hot starch vigorously in a mortar (or process in a heavy-duty mixer) until smooth and stretchy.
Wet hands periodically to shape the fufu into smooth balls.
Serve alongside soup or stew for scooping.

dishes.name: Attiéké
dishes.description: Fermented, granulated cassava staple, similar in texture to couscous.
steps: Sprinkle water lightly over the dried fermented cassava granules to rehydrate them.
Let it sit for a few minutes to absorb the moisture.
Steam the moistened granules for about 15-20 minutes until fluffy.
Fluff with a fork to separate the grains.
Serve alongside grilled fish or vegetables.

dishes.name: Kedjenou
dishes.description: Slow-simmered chicken stew cooked in a sealed clay pot for concentrated flavor.
steps: Combine chicken, tomato, onion, pepper, and ginger in a heavy pot with a tight-fitting lid.
Seal the pot tightly (traditionally with dough around the lid) to trap all the steam.
Cook over very low heat, shaking the pot occasionally instead of stirring, for about an hour.
Check that the chicken is fully tender before serving.
Serve with attieke or rice.

dishes.name: Groundnut Stew
dishes.description: Rich, nutty stew found across West Africa, built on a peanut paste base.
steps: Brown the meat with onion until lightly colored.
Add crushed tomato and chili, simmering for 10 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter and enough water to reach a stew-like consistency.
Simmer gently, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, until the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.
Serve over rice or with fufu.

dishes.name: Akara
dishes.description: Deep-fried bean fritters, a popular Nigerian breakfast food.
steps: Blend soaked and peeled black-eyed peas with onion and pepper into a thick, airy batter.
Whip the batter by hand or with a mixer until light and fluffy.
Heat oil until hot.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the oil and fry until deeply golden on all sides.
Drain and serve hot.

dishes.name: Efo Riro
dishes.description: Rich Yoruba vegetable soup made with leafy greens and palm oil.
steps: Sauté onion and blended pepper in palm oil until fragrant.
Add cooked assorted meat or fish and simmer briefly to absorb the flavors.
Add the leafy greens in batches, letting each wilt before adding more.
Simmer until the greens are tender but still vibrant, about 10 minutes.
Serve with pounded yam or rice.

dishes.name: Ndolé
dishes.description: Cameroon's national dish, combining bitter leaves with a nutty peanut sauce.
steps: Simmer bitter leaves (or substitute spinach) to reduce bitterness, changing the water if needed.
Cook meat or fish separately until tender.
Blend or stir ground peanuts with a little water into a smooth paste.
Combine the peanut paste, greens, and meat, simmering together until thickened, about 30 minutes.
Add dried shrimp partway through for extra depth.

dishes.name: Mafé
dishes.description: West African peanut stew, hearty and slightly sweet from the groundnut base.
steps: Brown beef cubes with onion.
Stir in tomato paste and cook briefly.
Add peanut butter thinned with water, stirring until smooth.
Add sweet potato and simmer covered until the meat and vegetables are tender, about an hour.
Serve over rice.

dishes.name: Nshima
dishes.description: Stiff maize porridge, Zambia's staple starch, eaten with relishes.
steps: Bring water to a boil.
Mix a portion of maize flour with cold water to make a paste, then stir it into the boiling water.
Cook, stirring, until it thickens.
Gradually add remaining flour, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon until very stiff and smooth.
Shape into a mound and serve with vegetables or stew.

dishes.name: Sadza
dishes.description: Zimbabwe's staple maize porridge, similar to ugali and nshima.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Stir in a portion of maize flour to form a loose porridge, and cook a few minutes.
Gradually add the remaining flour, stirring constantly and vigorously.
Continue cooking and stirring until very thick and smooth, about 10 minutes.
Shape into a mound and serve with relish or stew.

dishes.name: Moambe Chicken
dishes.description: Chicken stewed in a rich palm nut sauce, widely considered a Congolese national dish.
steps: Brown chicken pieces with onion.
Add tomato and chili, cooking until softened.
Stir in palm nut cream (or palm oil with a little tomato paste as a substitute) and enough water to make a sauce.
Simmer until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened, about 40 minutes.
Serve with rice or fufu.

dishes.name: Matapa
dishes.description: Mozambican stew of cassava leaves cooked with ground peanuts and coconut milk.
steps: Simmer chopped cassava leaves (or spinach) in a little water until tender.
Stir in ground peanuts and coconut milk.
Add shrimp or crab and garlic, simmering until the seafood is cooked through.
Continue simmering until the sauce thickens slightly, about 20 minutes.
Serve with rice.

dishes.name: Potjiekos
key_ingredients: slow-cooked in a cast iron pot
dishes.description: South African stew slow-cooked over coals in a three-legged cast iron pot.
steps: Brown meat in a cast iron pot over coals.
Layer onion, carrot, and potato on top of the meat without stirring.
Add stock, cover, and let cook slowly over low coals for several hours without stirring.
Check occasionally and add more liquid if needed.
Serve directly from the pot once the meat and vegetables are tender.

dishes.name: Vetkoek
dishes.description: South African fried dough bread, often stuffed with spiced mince or jam.
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let it foam.
Mix with flour into a soft dough and let rise for about an hour.
Divide into balls and let rest briefly.
Deep fry until puffed and golden brown all over.
Split open and fill with spiced mince or jam.

dishes.name: Matoke
dishes.description: Steamed and mashed green bananas, a staple across the African Great Lakes region.
steps: Peel green bananas and wrap them in their own leaves or foil.
Steam over low heat for about an hour until very soft.
Mash the steamed bananas lightly.
Sauté onion and tomato separately, then fold into the mashed matoke, or serve the sauce over it.
Serve warm as a starchy side.

dishes.name: Luwombo
dishes.description: Ugandan stew steamed inside banana leaves for a distinct aroma.
steps: Brown the meat with onion, then combine with groundnut sauce.
Wrap the mixture tightly in banana leaves, tying them securely.
Steam the wrapped parcels for 1.5-2 hours until the meat is tender.
Unwrap carefully to release the aromatic steam.
Serve with rice or matoke.

dishes.name: Swahili Pilau
dishes.description: Fragrant spiced rice dish from the East African coast, influenced by Indian and Arab trade.
steps: Brown meat with onion and pilau masala until fragrant.
Add stock and simmer until the meat is nearly tender.
Add rice, stirring to coat in the spiced broth.
Cover and cook on low heat until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid, about 20 minutes.
Fluff and serve.

dishes.name: Mandazi
dishes.description: Lightly sweet East African fried bread, similar to a doughnut.
steps: Dissolve yeast in a little warm coconut milk.
Mix flour, sugar, cardamom, and the yeast mixture with remaining coconut milk into a soft dough.
Let rise for about an hour.
Roll out and cut into triangles or rounds.
Deep fry until puffed and golden on both sides.

dishes.name: Kachumbari
dishes.description: Fresh, tangy tomato and onion salad served alongside grilled meats.
steps: Dice tomato and onion into small, even pieces.
Combine with minced chili and chopped cilantro.
Dress with fresh lime juice.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve fresh alongside grilled meats.

dishes.name: Hoppers (Appa)
dishes.description: Bowl-shaped fermented rice pancakes, often with an egg cooked in the center.
steps: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, yeast, and sugar into a thin batter, then let it ferment for a few hours.
Heat a small curved hopper pan and swirl a ladle of batter around the sides to form a thin bowl shape.
Crack an egg into the center if making egg hoppers.
Cover and cook until the edges are crisp and lacy and the center is set.
Gently remove and serve immediately.

dishes.name: Kottu Roti
dishes.description: Sri Lankan street food of chopped roti stir-fried with vegetables and curry.
steps: Chop cooked flatbread into small strips.
Stir-fry mixed vegetables and egg on a hot flat griddle.
Add the chopped roti to the griddle along with curry sauce.
Toss and chop everything together vigorously using two flat blades (or spatulas), a signature technique.
Serve hot straight off the griddle.

dishes.name: Momo
dishes.description: Steamed or fried dumplings popular across Nepal and the Himalayas.
steps: Make a simple dough from flour and water, then rest it.
Mix ground meat or vegetables with minced onion, ginger, and garlic.
Roll dough into small rounds and fill each with a spoonful of filling.
Pleat and pinch closed into small dumplings.
Steam for 10-12 minutes until cooked through, and serve with a spicy tomato-based dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Dal Bhat
dishes.description: Nepal's everyday meal of lentil soup, rice, and vegetables.
steps: Cook lentils with turmeric until soft, then temper with cumin fried in ghee.
Cook rice separately until fluffy.
Prepare a simple vegetable curry on the side.
Plate rice with the lentil dal and vegetable curry.
Serve with a pickle (achar) on the side, as is traditional.

dishes.name: Rogan Josh
dishes.description: Deep red, aromatic Kashmiri lamb curry.
steps: Brown lamb pieces in ghee, then set aside.
Sauté onion until deeply golden.
Add kashmiri chili and fennel powder, cooking until fragrant.
Return the lamb, stir in yogurt gradually to prevent curdling, then add water to cover.
Cover and simmer 1-1.5 hours until the lamb is tender and the sauce is deep red and thick.

dishes.name: Vindaloo
dishes.description: Fiery, tangy Goan curry with Portuguese roots.
steps: Blend vinegar, chilies, garlic, ginger, and mustard seeds into a smooth marinade paste.
Marinate the pork in this paste for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Brown the marinated pork in a hot pot.
Add a little water and simmer covered for 1-1.5 hours until tender.
Uncover and reduce the sauce to the desired thickness before serving.

dishes.name: Dhokla
dishes.description: Steamed, spongy savory cake from Gujarat.

ingredients.name: eno fruit salt or baking soda

ingredient_names: eno fruit salt or baking soda
steps: Whisk chickpea flour with yogurt and water into a smooth, thick batter, then let it ferment or rest 20 minutes.
Stir in the eno or baking soda just before steaming, which activates and aerates the batter.
Pour into a greased pan and steam for 15-20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil, then pour over the steamed cake.
Cut into squares and serve with green chutney.

dishes.name: Pav Bhaji
dishes.description: Buttery mashed vegetable curry served with soft bread rolls, a Mumbai street food icon.
steps: Boil mixed vegetables until very soft, then mash roughly.
Sauté onion in butter until soft, then add tomato and pav bhaji masala.
Add the mashed vegetables and simmer, mashing further as it cooks, until thick.
Toast the pav rolls in butter on a griddle.
Serve the bhaji topped with a pat of butter alongside the toasted rolls.

dishes.name: Chole Bhature
dishes.description: Spiced chickpeas served with fluffy deep-fried bread.
steps: Sauté onion and tomato with chole masala until it forms a thick base.
Add cooked chickpeas and simmer 15-20 minutes, mashing a few for texture.
Make bhature dough from flour, yogurt, and a little baking powder, resting it for an hour.
Roll and deep-fry the dough until puffed and golden.
Serve the chickpea curry hot alongside the fried bread.

dishes.name: Idli Sambar
dishes.description: Soft steamed rice cakes served with a tangy lentil stew, a South Indian breakfast staple.

ingredients.name: idli rice and urad dal batter

ingredient_names: idli rice and urad dal batter
steps: Pour fermented idli batter into greased molds and steam for 10-12 minutes until fluffy.
Meanwhile, cook toor dal until soft and mash it.
Sauté vegetables, then add tamarind paste, sambar powder, and the cooked dal with water to make a stew.
Simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Serve the steamed idli with hot sambar and coconut chutney.

dishes.name: Aloo Gobi
dishes.description: Simple, popular dry-spiced potato and cauliflower dish.
steps: Heat oil and sizzle cumin seeds until fragrant.
Add ginger, then potato and cauliflower.
Stir in turmeric and a little salt, coating the vegetables evenly.
Cover and cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes.
Finish with fresh cilantro before serving.

dishes.name: Chow Mein
dishes.description: Crispy or soft stir-fried noodles with vegetables and often meat.
steps: Parboil or soak noodles until just tender, then drain well.
Stir-fry sliced vegetables and protein in a hot wok.
Push everything to the side and add the noodles directly to the hot wok surface to get some char.
Toss everything together with soy sauce and a little sesame oil.
Serve immediately while hot.

dishes.name: Congee
dishes.description: Comforting rice porridge, eaten across East Asia with savory toppings.
steps: Combine rice and water or stock in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a very low simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 1-1.5 hours until the rice breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge.
Add water as needed if it becomes too thick.
Serve topped with scallion, a soft egg, or preserved vegetables.

dishes.name: Jiaozi (Chinese Dumplings)
dishes.description: Boiled, steamed, or pan-fried dumplings, essential to Lunar New Year meals.
steps: Mix ground pork with minced cabbage, scallion, ginger, and soy sauce.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each dumpling wrapper.
Fold and pleat the edges to seal.
Boil, steam, or pan-fry (potstickers) until cooked through.
Serve with a dipping sauce of soy sauce, vinegar, and chili oil.

dishes.name: Spring Rolls
dishes.description: Crispy fried rolls filled with vegetables or meat.
steps: Stir-fry shredded cabbage, carrot, and mushroom until just softened, then let cool.
Place a spoonful of the vegetable filling on each wrapper.
Roll tightly, folding in the sides, and seal the edge with a little water or flour paste.
Deep fry until golden and crisp.
Serve with a sweet chili or soy dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Buuz
dishes.description: Mongolian steamed meat dumplings, traditionally eaten during Lunar New Year.
steps: Make a simple dough from flour and water and rest it.
Mix ground meat with minced onion and a little water to keep it juicy.
Roll dough into small rounds and fill with the meat mixture.
Pleat closed at the top into a small pouch.
Steam for 15-20 minutes until the meat is cooked through.

dishes.name: Khorkhog
dishes.description: Mongolian barbecue where meat is cooked with hot stones in a sealed pot.

ingredients.name: hot stones (or a heavy sealed pot)

ingredient_names: hot stones (or a heavy sealed pot)
steps: Heat stones over an open fire until very hot (or heat a heavy sealed pot as a substitute).
Layer meat, vegetables, and hot stones alternately in a large sealed vessel.
Seal tightly and cook over the fire, shaking occasionally, until the meat is very tender, about 1.5-2 hours.
Open carefully, as steam will be intense.
Serve the meat and vegetables together, traditionally passing the warm stones as a hand-warmer.

dishes.name: Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup
dishes.description: Rich, soy-braised beef broth over hand-pulled noodles.
steps: Braise beef shank in soy sauce, star anise, and aromatics until very tender, about 2 hours.
Strain the braising liquid to use as the soup base, adding more stock as needed.
Cook wheat noodles separately until tender.
Slice the braised beef.
Assemble bowls with noodles, broth, sliced beef, and scallion.

dishes.name: Gua Bao
dishes.description: Fluffy steamed bun folded around braised pork belly.
steps: Braise pork belly in soy sauce and spices until very tender, then slice.
Steam the buns until soft and fluffy.
Open each bun and fill with a slice of braised pork belly.
Add pickled mustard greens and a sprinkle of crushed peanuts.
Serve warm.

dishes.name: Hong Kong Egg Tart
dishes.description: Hong Kong's take on the Portuguese egg tart, with a lighter custard.
steps: Line small tart tins with pastry.
Whisk eggs, sugar, and evaporated milk together until smooth, then strain.
Pour the custard into the pastry shells.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until the custard is just set with a slight jiggle, about 15-18 minutes.
Cool before serving, as the custard firms up while cooling.

dishes.name: Fish Amok
dishes.description: Cambodia's national dish: fish steamed in coconut curry inside a banana leaf.
steps: Mix kroeung paste with coconut milk and beaten egg to make a light custard base.
Fold in chunks of fish.
Line small bowls or folded banana leaf cups with extra banana leaf.
Spoon the fish mixture into the cups.
Steam for 20-25 minutes until just set.

dishes.name: Lok Lak
dishes.description: Stir-fried marinated beef cubes served over salad with a tangy dipping sauce.
steps: Marinate beef cubes in garlic, soy sauce, and a little sugar for 20 minutes.
Sear the beef quickly in a very hot pan or wok until browned but still tender.
Toss with oyster sauce just before removing from heat.
Serve over a bed of lettuce and sliced tomato.
Serve with lime pepper dipping sauce on the side.

dishes.name: Larb
dishes.description: Spicy, herby minced meat salad, considered Laos' national dish.
steps: Cook ground meat in a dry pan, breaking it into small crumbles, until just cooked through.
Toss the warm meat with fish sauce and lime juice.
Stir in toasted rice powder for texture and nutty flavor.
Fold in torn mint and cilantro just before serving.
Serve with sticky rice and fresh cabbage leaves.

dishes.name: Mohinga
dishes.description: Myanmar's beloved breakfast fish noodle soup.
steps: Simmer whole fish with lemongrass and aromatics until cooked, then remove bones and flake the meat.
Return the flaked fish to the broth along with banana stem.
Whisk in a little chickpea flour to slightly thicken the broth.
Cook rice noodles separately.
Assemble bowls with noodles, hot broth, and crispy fritters or boiled egg on top.

dishes.name: Tea Leaf Salad
dishes.description: Distinctive Burmese salad built on fermented tea leaves.
steps: Combine fermented tea leaves with a little oil and lime juice.
Add diced tomato and shredded cabbage.
Toss with fried garlic, fried beans, and crushed peanuts.
Season with a splash of fish sauce and more lime juice.
Toss everything together just before serving so it stays crunchy.

dishes.name: Nasi Lemak
dishes.description: Malaysia's national dish: fragrant coconut rice with spicy sambal and sides.
steps: Cook rice in coconut milk with a pandan leaf for fragrance.
Make sambal by frying blended chili paste with onion and a little sugar until deeply reduced.
Fry anchovies and peanuts until crisp.
Boil an egg.
Plate the coconut rice with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, egg, and cucumber slices.

dishes.name: Char Kway Teow
dishes.description: Smoky wok-fried flat noodles, a hawker classic.

ingredients.name: soy sauce and dark soy sauce

ingredient_names: soy sauce and dark soy sauce
steps: Heat a wok until smoking hot with oil.
Stir-fry shrimp briefly, then push to the side.
Add noodles and sauces, tossing constantly over high heat for that signature smoky flavor.
Push noodles aside, scramble an egg, then combine everything.
Fold in bean sprouts at the very end and serve immediately.

dishes.name: Roti Canai
dishes.description: Flaky, layered flatbread griddled fresh, usually served with curry.
steps: Make a soft, oiled dough and rest it for at least an hour, ideally longer.
Flatten and stretch each portion of dough very thin by hand, almost translucent.
Fold the stretched dough into a coil or square.
Griddle in ghee until golden and flaky on both sides, pressing gently to create layers.
Serve warm with dhal or curry for dipping.

dishes.name: Pancit
dishes.description: Filipino noodle dish traditionally served at birthdays for long life.
steps: Soak noodles until softened, then drain.
Stir-fry chicken and shrimp until cooked through, then set aside.
Sauté mixed vegetables briefly.
Add the noodles with soy sauce and a little broth, tossing to combine.
Return the meat to the pan, toss everything together, and serve with a squeeze of calamansi or lime.

dishes.name: Sinigang
dishes.description: Sour tamarind-based Filipino soup, a comfort food staple.
steps: Simmer pork or shrimp with tomato and onion until nearly cooked.
Add tamarind soup base (or fresh tamarind) for the signature sour flavor.
Add radish and other vegetables, simmering until tender.
Add water spinach or other leafy greens near the end so they stay bright.
Season with fish sauce and serve hot with rice.

dishes.name: Lechon
dishes.description: Whole spit-roasted pig with crackling skin, centerpiece of Filipino celebrations.
steps: Stuff the cavity of the pig with lemongrass and garlic.
Season the skin generously with salt.
Skewer the pig on a large rotisserie spit.
Roast slowly over charcoal for several hours, turning constantly, until the skin is deeply crackling and the meat is tender.
Carve and serve with a liver-based dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Halo-Halo
dishes.description: Layered shaved ice dessert loaded with sweet toppings and ube ice cream.
steps: Layer sweet beans, jackfruit, and other preserved fruits at the bottom of a tall glass.
Pile shaved ice generously on top.
Pour evaporated milk over the ice.
Top with a scoop of ube ice cream and a slice of leche flan.
Mix everything together before eating.

dishes.name: Gỏi Cuốn (Fresh Spring Rolls)
dishes.description: Fresh, unfried rice paper rolls filled with herbs, shrimp, and noodles.
steps: Cook vermicelli and drain.
Soften a rice paper wrapper briefly in warm water.
Layer lettuce, herbs, vermicelli, and shrimp near the bottom edge.
Roll tightly, folding in the sides as you go.
Serve fresh with peanut dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Khao Soi
dishes.description: Northern Thai curry noodle soup topped with crispy fried noodles.
steps: Fry curry paste in a little coconut cream until fragrant.
Add chicken and the rest of the coconut milk, simmering until the chicken is cooked through.
Cook fresh egg noodles and divide into bowls.
Ladle the curry broth and chicken over the noodles.
Top with crispy fried noodles, pickled mustard greens, and a squeeze of lime.

dishes.name: Meat Pie
dishes.description: Individual-sized savory pie filled with minced meat and gravy, an Australian icon.
steps: Brown ground beef with diced onion.
Stir in gravy and simmer until thick and rich.
Let the filling cool, then spoon into pastry-lined individual pie tins.
Top with another layer of pastry, sealing the edges and venting the top.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) until the pastry is puffed and golden, about 25 minutes.

dishes.name: Pavlova
dishes.description: Crisp-shelled, marshmallowy meringue dessert topped with fruit and cream.
steps: Whip egg whites to soft peaks, then gradually add sugar, whipping to stiff, glossy peaks.
Fold in cornstarch and vinegar gently.
Shape the meringue into a large round on a lined baking sheet, building up the sides slightly.
Bake at a low temperature (250°F/120°C) for about 1.5 hours, then let cool completely in the oven.
Top with whipped cream and fresh fruit just before serving.

dishes.name: Vegemite on Toast
dishes.description: Simple Australian breakfast built on the famously polarizing yeast spread.
steps: Toast the bread until golden.
Spread a thin layer of butter while still warm.
Add a very thin layer of vegemite (it's intensely salty, so less is more).
Spread evenly to the edges.
Serve immediately while the toast is warm.

dishes.name: Hāngī
dishes.description: Māori method of cooking food in a pit oven with heated stones.
steps: Heat stones in a large pit fire until glowing hot.
Wrap meats and vegetables separately in leaves or foil.
Place the wrapped food over the hot stones in the pit.
Cover everything with earth or a heavy covering to trap the steam completely.
Let cook undisturbed for 3-4 hours, then carefully uncover and serve.

dishes.name: Poke
dishes.description: Diced raw fish salad, a Hawaiian staple now popular worldwide.
steps: Cut very fresh raw fish (typically ahi tuna) into cubes.
Toss with soy sauce, sesame oil, and chopped scallion.
Add other mix-ins like seaweed, onion, or macadamia nuts.
Let marinate briefly in the fridge, 10-15 minutes.
Serve over rice or on its own.

dishes.name: Kalua Pig
dishes.description: Whole pig slow-roasted in an underground imu oven, a luau centerpiece.
steps: Rub the pork generously with sea salt.
Wrap tightly in banana leaves.
Traditionally, bury with hot stones in an underground pit (imu); alternatively, slow roast at 275°F (135°C) wrapped tightly.
Cook low and slow for 6-8 hours until completely tender.
Shred the meat and serve with its juices.

dishes.name: Pabellón Criollo
dishes.description: Venezuela's national dish combining shredded beef, beans, rice, and plantain.
steps: Simmer beef until very tender, then shred it and simmer briefly in a light tomato sauce.
Cook black beans with onion and garlic until flavorful.
Cook white rice separately.
Fry sliced ripe plantain until caramelized.
Plate the rice, beans, shredded beef, and plantain together in separate sections.

dishes.name: Cachapa
dishes.description: Sweet corn pancake, often folded around soft cheese.
steps: Blend fresh corn kernels with a little cornmeal and sugar into a thick batter.
Cook ladlefuls on a hot griddle like a pancake until set and lightly golden.
Flip and cook the other side.
Fold a slice of soft cheese into the warm cachapa.
Serve immediately while warm and the cheese is melting.

dishes.name: Bandeja Paisa
dishes.description: Massive Colombian platter combining beans, rice, meats, and egg.
steps: Cook red beans with pork until tender and flavorful.
Cook rice separately.
Grill or fry chorizo and season ground beef, cooking until browned.
Fry eggs and slice avocado.
Arrange all components on a large platter alongside fried plantain and arepa.

dishes.name: Ajiaco
dishes.description: Bogotá's hearty chicken and potato soup, made with a native Andean herb.

ingredients.name: corn on the cob, cut into pieces

ingredient_names: corn on the cob, cut into pieces
steps: Simmer chicken in a large pot of water with onion and garlic until tender.
Remove chicken, shred it, and set aside.
Add all three types of potato to the broth, cooking until some break down to thicken the soup while others hold their shape.
Add corn and guasca herb, simmering until the corn is tender.
Return shredded chicken to the pot and serve with capers and cream on the side.

dishes.name: Llapingachos
dishes.description: Cheese-stuffed potato patties, a staple of Ecuadorian cuisine.
steps: Mash boiled potato with achiote oil for color and flavor.
Mix in shredded cheese.
Shape the mixture into patties.
Griddle the patties in a little oil until golden and crisp on both sides.
Serve with peanut sauce, fried egg, and salad.

dishes.name: Encebollado
dishes.description: Ecuadorian fish and cassava soup, popular as a hangover cure.
steps: Simmer fish in water with onion and tomato until just cooked, then flake it.
Cook yuca chunks in the same broth until very tender.
Combine the flaked fish and yuca back into the broth.
Top generously with pickled red onion.
Serve hot with lime and popcorn or plantain chips on the side, as is traditional.

dishes.name: Salteñas
dishes.description: Bolivian baked empanada-like pastry filled with juicy, slightly sweet stew.

ingredients.name: beef or chicken stew, thick and slightly sweet

ingredient_names: beef or chicken stew, thick and slightly sweet
steps: Make a stew filling that's thicker and slightly sweeter than a typical empanada filling, then chill it until very firm (this prevents leaks).
Roll dough into rounds.
Place a spoonful of the cold, jellied filling along with egg, olives, and raisins onto each round.
Fold and crimp the edges into a distinctive braided seal.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until golden, about 20-25 minutes.

dishes.name: Asado Uruguayo
dishes.description: Uruguay's version of the South American barbecue tradition.
steps: Build a wood fire and let it burn down to steady embers.
Season the meat simply with coarse salt.
Grill slowly over indirect heat, turning occasionally, until deeply browned and cooked through.
Grill chorizo alongside until browned and cooked.
Rest briefly before serving with chimichurri or salad.

dishes.name: Chivito
dishes.description: Loaded Uruguayan steak sandwich piled with toppings.
steps: Grill the steak until cooked to preference.
Layer ham and cheese over the hot steak so the cheese melts slightly.
Fry eggs sunny-side up.
Toast the bread rolls.
Stack the steak, ham, cheese, egg, and toppings like lettuce and tomato into the roll.

dishes.name: Ropa Vieja
dishes.description: Cuba's national dish of slow-cooked shredded beef in tomato sauce.
steps: Simmer flank steak in water with onion and bay leaf until very tender, about 1.5-2 hours.
Shred the cooked beef with two forks.
Sauté bell pepper and onion until soft.
Add tomato sauce, cumin, and the shredded beef, simmering together until well combined.
Serve with rice and black beans.

dishes.name: Moros y Cristianos
dishes.description: Cuban black beans and rice cooked together, named for their contrasting colors.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic with cumin until fragrant.
Add cooked black beans with a little of their liquid.
Add rice and enough water or broth to cook it.
Cover and simmer until the rice is tender and has absorbed the bean liquid, taking on a deep color.
Fluff and serve.

dishes.name: Mangú
dishes.description: Mashed boiled plantains, a Dominican breakfast staple.
steps: Boil peeled green plantains in salted water until very soft.
Mash the hot plantains with a little of the cooking water and butter until smooth.
Sauté sliced onion in oil with a splash of vinegar until soft and tangy.
Spread the pickled onions over the mashed plantain.
Serve warm, often with fried cheese, eggs, and salami.

dishes.name: Sancocho
dishes.description: Hearty root vegetable and meat stew found in many Latin American countries, with regional variations.
steps: Simmer the mixed meats in a large pot of water with onion and garlic until tender.
Add yuca, corn, plantain, and other root vegetables.
Simmer until all the vegetables are tender and the broth is rich and flavorful, about an hour total.
Skim any excess fat from the surface.
Serve hot in deep bowls with rice on the side.

dishes.name: Pepián
dishes.description: Guatemala's national dish, a stew thickened with toasted spices and seeds.
steps: Toast sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, and dried chilies in a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend the toasted seeds and chilies with tomato into a smooth sauce.
Brown chicken pieces, then add the blended sauce and enough water to cover.
Add potato and simmer until the chicken and potato are tender, about 40 minutes.
Serve with rice.

dishes.name: Baleada
dishes.description: Simple, beloved Honduran folded tortilla with beans and cheese.
steps: Warm the flour tortillas on a griddle.
Spread a generous layer of refried beans over half of each tortilla.
Add crumbled cheese and a drizzle of crema.
Fold the tortilla in half.
Serve warm, optionally with scrambled egg or avocado added.

dishes.name: Gallo Pinto
dishes.description: Central American breakfast staple of rice and beans cooked together.
steps: Sauté onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add cooked black beans along with a little of their liquid.
Add the cooked rice, stirring to combine and coat the grains in the bean liquid.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until everything is well combined and slightly darker in color.
Serve for breakfast, often with eggs and plantain.

dishes.name: Casado
dishes.description: Costa Rican combination plate, literally 'married' rice, beans, and sides.
steps: Cook rice and beans separately, seasoned simply.
Fry ripe plantain slices until caramelized.
Prepare a simple shredded cabbage and tomato salad.
Grill or pan-fry the chosen protein.
Plate all the components together on one large plate, in the traditional combination-plate style.

dishes.name: Griot
dishes.description: Haitian fried pork, marinated in citrus and served with spicy pickled slaw.
steps: Marinate pork cubes in sour orange juice, garlic, and scotch bonnet for at least 2 hours.
Simmer the pork in its marinade with a little water until tender, about 45 minutes.
Drain the pork, reserving the liquid.
Fry the tender pork pieces in hot oil until deeply browned and crispy outside.
Serve with pikliz and fried plantain.

dishes.name: Pikliz
dishes.description: Fiery Haitian pickled cabbage relish, served alongside fried dishes.
steps: Combine shredded cabbage, carrot, and scotch bonnet in a large jar.
Pack the vegetables tightly.
Pour white vinegar over the top until fully submerged.
Seal and let sit at room temperature for at least 24 hours before using.
Store refrigerated; it keeps for weeks and grows tangier over time.

dishes.name: Pastel de Choclo
dishes.description: Chilean corn pie layered over a savory beef filling.
steps: Cook ground beef with onion and warming spices for the filling.
Blend fresh corn with a little milk and sugar into a thick, slightly sweet puree.
Spread the beef filling with olives and egg pieces in the bottom of a baking dish.
Top with the corn puree in an even layer.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until the top is golden, about 30-35 minutes.

dishes.name: Curanto
dishes.description: Traditional Chilote dish of seafood and meat slow-cooked underground.
steps: Heat stones in a pit fire until very hot.
Layer shellfish, meats, and potatoes with large leaves separating each layer.
Cover the pit completely to trap steam.
Let cook undisturbed for 1.5-2 hours.
Uncover carefully and serve everything together.

dishes.name: Empanada de Pino
dishes.description: Chile's baked empanada filled with spiced beef, olives, and egg.
steps: Cook ground beef slowly with a generous amount of diced onion until the onion nearly melts into the meat.
Let the filling cool completely.
Place filling with a slice of egg and an olive onto each pastry disc.
Fold into a half-moon and crimp the edges into a decorative seal.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until golden, about 25-30 minutes.

dishes.name: Doubles
dishes.description: Trinidad's beloved street food of curried chickpeas sandwiched in fried bread.
steps: Make a soft, turmeric-tinted yeasted dough and let it rise.
Flatten small portions into thin rounds and fry briefly until puffed (these are the 'bara').
Prepare a curried chickpea filling, seasoned with curry powder and pepper.
Sandwich a spoonful of curried chickpeas between two bara.
Serve with tamarind and pepper sauces.

dishes.name: Trinidadian Roti
dishes.description: Soft flatbread wrapped around curry, reflecting Trinidad's Indian heritage.
steps: Make a soft dough from flour, water, and a little ghee, then rest it.
Roll into large thin rounds and griddle, brushing with ghee, until cooked through and flaky.
Prepare a curry filling of choice.
Spoon the curry into the center of the roti.
Fold the roti around the filling like a parcel and serve warm.

dishes.name: Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
dishes.description: Barbados' national dish pairing a cornmeal-okra mash with steamed fish.
steps: Simmer sliced okra in water until soft.
Gradually whisk in cornmeal, stirring constantly to avoid lumps, until it forms a thick, smooth mash.
Season fish with lime and spices, then steam or poach until just cooked through.
Shape the cou-cou into a mound.
Serve alongside the steamed fish and a light gravy.

dishes.name: Ackee and Saltfish
dishes.description: Jamaica's national dish, combining a unique local fruit with salted fish.
steps: Soak salted cod to remove excess salt, then flake it.
Sauté onion, tomato, and pepper.
Add the flaked saltfish and cook briefly.
Gently fold in ackee (careful not to break it up too much) and warm through.
Serve with fried dumplings or breadfruit.

dishes.name: Curry Goat
dishes.description: Jamaican slow-cooked curried goat, a centerpiece of celebrations.
steps: Marinate goat meat in curry powder, garlic, and thyme for several hours or overnight.
Brown the meat in oil with scotch bonnet pepper.
Add water or stock and simmer slowly until the meat is very tender, 1.5-2 hours.
Add potato partway through and cook until soft.
Serve with rice and peas.

dishes.name: Jambalaya
dishes.description: Louisiana Creole rice dish loaded with meat and the holy trinity of vegetables.
steps: Sauté the trinity (onion, celery, bell pepper) with sausage until browned.
Add rice and toast briefly in the fat.
Add broth, tomato, and Cajun spices, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until the rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in shrimp or chicken near the end and cook through.

dishes.name: Lobster Roll
dishes.description: Chilled or buttered lobster meat served in a toasted split-top bun.
steps: Steam or boil lobster until just cooked through, then cool and chop the meat.
Toss the lobster meat lightly with mayonnaise (or melted butter for a warm version), keeping it chunky.
Season with a squeeze of lemon and a little celery for crunch, if desired.
Toast a split-top hot dog bun with butter until golden.
Pile the lobster salad into the toasted bun and serve immediately.

dishes.name: Philly Cheesesteak
dishes.description: Philadelphia's iconic sandwich of griddled beef and cheese.
steps: Thinly slice ribeye or use pre-shaved beef.
Griddle the beef with sliced onion until cooked through, chopping it into smaller pieces as it cooks.
Melt cheese (traditionally Cheez Whiz or provolone) directly over the meat on the griddle.
Scoop the meat and melted cheese into a long hoagie roll.
Serve hot, with or without peppers.

dishes.name: Chicago Deep Dish Pizza
dishes.description: Pizza baked in a deep pan with cheese under a chunky tomato sauce.
steps: Press thick dough into a deep, well-oiled pan, pushing it up the sides.
Layer sliced mozzarella directly onto the dough.
Add cooked crumbled sausage over the cheese.
Pour crushed tomato sauce over the top (sauce goes on last in Chicago style).
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 30-35 minutes until the crust is golden and cooked through.

dishes.name: Fajitas
dishes.description: Sizzling grilled meat and pepper strips wrapped in warm tortillas.
steps: Marinate the meat in lime juice, garlic, and spices for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or sear the meat until charred outside and cooked to preference, then slice.
Sauté bell pepper and onion until slightly charred but still crisp.
Warm the tortillas.
Serve the sliced meat and vegetables sizzling hot with warm tortillas and toppings.

dishes.name: Texas Brisket
dishes.description: Slow-smoked beef brisket, the centerpiece of Texas barbecue.
steps: Coat the brisket generously with dry rub.
Smoke at a low, steady temperature (225-250°F/107-121°C) for 10-14 hours until it reaches a tender internal texture.
Wrap in butcher paper partway through smoking to help retain moisture.
Rest the brisket for at least 30 minutes before slicing.
Slice against the grain and serve.

dishes.name: Shrimp and Grits
dishes.description: Creamy corn grits topped with seasoned shrimp, a Southern breakfast classic.
steps: Bring water or stock to a boil, then whisk in grits gradually.
Simmer, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 20-25 minutes.
Stir in butter and cheese until melted and smooth.
Sauté seasoned shrimp in a separate pan until just pink.
Spoon shrimp and their pan sauce over the hot grits to serve.

dishes.name: Butter Tart
dishes.description: Small, gooey Canadian pastry tart with a caramel-like filling.
steps: Line small tart tins with pastry dough.
Melt butter and whisk with brown sugar and eggs until smooth.
Add a few raisins to the bottom of each tart shell if using.
Pour the filling into the shells, filling about two-thirds full.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15-18 minutes until the filling is just set with a slight jiggle in the center.

dishes.name: Tourtière
dishes.description: Québécois meat pie traditionally served during the winter holidays.
steps: Cook ground pork with onion and warming spices until browned.
Stir in mashed potato to bind and thicken the filling.
Let the filling cool, then spoon into a pastry-lined pie dish.
Top with the second pastry disc, sealing and venting the top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for about 45 minutes until deeply golden.

dishes.name: Plov
dishes.description: Uzbekistan's national rice pilaf, cooked with lamb and carrots in one pot.
steps: Brown lamb cubes with onion in a heavy pot.
Add julienned carrot and cook until softened.
Stir in cumin and a little water, simmering until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add rice on top without stirring, then add enough water to just cover.
Cover and cook on low heat until the rice is tender, about 25 minutes, then fluff everything together.

dishes.name: Manti
dishes.description: Steamed dumplings found across Central Asia and Turkey, served with yogurt.
steps: Make a firm dough from flour and water, then rest it.
Mix ground meat with minced onion and seasoning.
Roll dough very thin and cut into small squares.
Place a small amount of filling in each square and pinch the corners together tightly.
Steam or boil until cooked through, then serve topped with yogurt-garlic sauce and a drizzle of paprika butter.

dishes.name: Lagman
dishes.description: Hand-pulled noodle dish with a spiced meat and vegetable topping.
steps: Stir-fry sliced meat until browned.
Add garlic, bell pepper, and tomato, cooking until softened into a light sauce.
Add a splash of stock and simmer briefly to bring the sauce together.
Cook hand-pulled (or substitute wide) noodles separately until tender.
Top the noodles generously with the meat and vegetable sauce.

dishes.name: Beshbarmak
dishes.description: Central Asian dish of boiled meat over noodles, traditionally eaten by hand.
steps: Simmer meat in water with onion until very tender, reserving the broth.
Cook flat pasta squares in the broth until tender.
Slice or shred the cooked meat.
Toss the noodles with some broth and top with sliced onion cooked briefly in the broth.
Arrange the meat over the noodles and serve with a cup of the hot broth on the side.

dishes.name: Khachapuri
dishes.description: Georgian cheese-filled bread, the boat-shaped version topped with a raw egg.
steps: Make a soft yeasted dough and let it rise.
Roll into an oval and pinch up the edges into a boat shape.
Fill with a mix of cheeses.
Bake until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Crack a raw egg into the center in the last few minutes so it cooks gently in the residual heat, then swirl in a pat of butter before serving.

dishes.name: Khinkali
dishes.description: Georgian soup dumplings, twisted at the top and held by the knot while eaten.
steps: Make a simple flour and water dough and rest it.
Mix ground meat with onion, garlic, and a little broth to keep it juicy.
Roll dough into rounds, add filling, and pleat the edges together into a twisted knot at the top.
Boil the dumplings until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Eat by holding the knot, biting a small opening, and sipping the broth inside before eating the rest.

dishes.name: Lobio
dishes.description: Georgian spiced bean stew, often flavored with walnuts and coriander.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Mash a portion of the cooked beans and combine with the whole beans for a mixed texture.
Stir in ground walnuts and sautéed onion.
Simmer briefly to combine flavors, adding a little bean cooking liquid if needed.
Finish with fresh cilantro and a drizzle of walnut oil.

dishes.name: Armenian Dolma
dishes.description: Stuffed grape leaves or vegetables, a staple across the Caucasus and Armenian diaspora.
steps: Mix rice with ground lamb, minced onion, and chopped herbs.
Place a spoonful of filling on each grape leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Layer the rolls snugly in a pot.
Add water or broth to just cover, weigh down with a plate, and simmer gently for about an hour.
Serve warm or at room temperature with yogurt.

dishes.name: Lavash
dishes.description: Thin, soft flatbread central to Armenian cuisine, baked in a clay oven.
steps: Mix flour, water, and salt into a firm, smooth dough, then rest it covered for 30 minutes.
Divide into small balls and roll each out very thin.
Cook on a very hot dry griddle or in a traditional clay oven (tandir) until lightly browned with a few char spots.
Stack the finished lavash and cover with a cloth to keep it soft.
Serve fresh alongside cheese, herbs, or grilled meats.

dishes.name: Masala Chai
dishes.description: Spiced milk tea, brewed strong and simmered with warming spices.
steps: Bring water to a boil with crushed cardamom and sliced ginger.
Add black tea leaves and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Add milk and sugar, bringing back to a gentle boil.
Simmer another 2-3 minutes until well infused and the color deepens.
Strain into cups and serve hot.

dishes.name: Lassi
dishes.description: Chilled yogurt drink, served sweet, salty, or fruit-flavored.
steps: Whisk yogurt with water or milk until smooth.
Add sugar for a sweet lassi, or salt and a pinch of roasted cumin for a savory one.
Blend briefly until frothy.
Chill well before serving.
Pour over ice and garnish as desired.

dishes.name: Bubble Tea
dishes.description: Taiwanese tea drink with chewy tapioca pearls, now a global phenomenon.
steps: Boil tapioca pearls according to package directions until soft and chewy, then soak in sugar syrup.
Brew strong black tea and let it cool slightly.
Combine tea, milk, and sweetener, stirring well.
Add a scoop of tapioca pearls to the bottom of each glass.
Pour the milk tea over the pearls and serve with a wide straw.

dishes.name: Caipirinha
dishes.description: Brazil's national cocktail, muddled lime and sugar cane spirit.
steps: Place lime quarters and sugar in a sturdy glass.
Muddle firmly to release the lime juice and oils.
Fill the glass with ice.
Pour in the cachaça.
Stir well and serve immediately.

dishes.name: Yerba Mate
dishes.description: Traditional caffeinated infusion shared communally through a metal straw.
steps: Fill a gourd about two-thirds full with yerba mate leaves.
Tilt the gourd to let the leaves settle to one side.
Insert the metal straw (bombilla) into the empty side.
Pour hot, not boiling, water slowly over the leaves.
Sip through the straw, refilling with hot water as it's finished, traditionally shared among a group.

dishes.name: Ayran
dishes.description: Savory, salted yogurt drink popular across Turkey and the Balkans.
steps: Whisk yogurt with cold water until smooth and well combined.
Add salt and whisk again.
Chill well before serving.
Whisk once more just before pouring, as it can separate slightly.
Serve very cold, ideally with a few ice cubes.

dishes.name: Kvass
dishes.description: Mildly alcoholic fermented rye bread beverage, a Slavic staple.
steps: Toast or dry out rye bread pieces in a low oven until very dark.
Steep the toasted bread in hot water for several hours.
Strain the liquid, then stir in sugar and a small amount of yeast.
Let ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days until lightly fizzy and tangy.
Strain again, bottle, and chill before serving.

dishes.name: Horchata
dishes.description: Sweet, milky rice and cinnamon drink served chilled.
steps: Soak rice with a cinnamon stick in water for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Blend the soaked rice and water until smooth.
Strain through a fine sieve or cheesecloth to remove solids.
Stir in condensed milk and vanilla.
Chill and serve over ice.

dishes.name: Turkish Coffee
dishes.description: Unfiltered coffee brewed slowly in a small pot, served with the grounds settled at the bottom.
steps: Combine finely ground coffee, cold water, and sugar (if using) in a small pot (cezve).
Stir well before heating.
Heat slowly over low heat, without stirring once it's on the heat.
Just as it begins to foam and rise, remove from heat, let it settle, then return briefly to heat once or twice more.
Pour into small cups, letting the grounds settle before drinking.

dishes.name: Moroccan Mint Tea
dishes.description: Sweet green tea steeped with fresh mint, poured from height to create froth.
steps: Rinse the green tea leaves briefly with a little boiling water, then discard that water.
Add fresh mint and sugar to the teapot with the tea leaves.
Pour in boiling water and let steep for 5 minutes.
Stir well to dissolve the sugar.
Pour from a height into small glasses to create a light froth.

dishes.name: Pisco Sour
dishes.description: Frothy South American cocktail built on grape brandy.
steps: Combine pisco, lime juice, simple syrup, and egg white in a shaker.
Dry shake (without ice) vigorously to emulsify the egg white.
Add ice and shake again until well chilled.
Strain into a glass.
Top with a couple dashes of bitters on the foam.

dishes.name: Michelada
dishes.description: Spicy, savory beer cocktail popular as a hangover cure.
steps: Rim a glass with salt and chili powder.
Fill the glass with ice.
Add lime juice, hot sauce, and worcestershire sauce.
Pour in cold beer.
Stir gently and serve immediately.

dishes.name: Rooibos Tea
dishes.description: Naturally caffeine-free red tea native to South Africa.
steps: Bring water to a boil.
Pour over rooibos leaves in a teapot or infuser.
Steep for 5-7 minutes, longer than typical tea, since rooibos is naturally mild.
Strain into cups.
Add milk and honey to taste if desired.

dishes.name: Chicha Morada
dishes.description: Sweet, spiced Peruvian drink made from purple corn.
steps: Simmer purple corn, pineapple rind, cinnamon, and cloves in a large pot of water for about an hour.
Strain out the solids, keeping the deep purple liquid.
Sweeten with sugar to taste while the liquid is still warm.
Add a good squeeze of lime juice.
Chill thoroughly and serve over ice.

dishes.name: Onigiri
dishes.description: Hand-formed rice balls wrapped in seaweed, a Japanese lunchbox staple.
steps: Wet your hands with lightly salted water to prevent sticking.
Take a handful of warm rice and flatten it in your palm.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center and fold the rice around it.
Shape firmly into a triangle or ball.
Wrap a strip of nori around the base before serving.

dishes.name: Chirashi Don
dishes.description: Bowl of sushi rice scattered with an assortment of fresh sashimi.
steps: Prepare and season sushi rice, then let it cool to room temperature.
Divide the rice between two bowls.
Arrange assorted sashimi slices attractively over the rice.
Garnish with pickled ginger and thin nori strips.
Serve immediately with soy sauce and wasabi on the side.

dishes.name: Yakisoba
dishes.description: Stir-fried wheat noodles in a tangy-sweet sauce, popular festival food.
steps: Stir-fry sliced pork until cooked through.
Add shredded cabbage and any other vegetables, cooking until just tender.
Add the noodles directly to the pan with a splash of water to loosen them.
Pour in the yakisoba sauce and toss everything together until evenly coated.
Top with pickled ginger before serving.

dishes.name: Oyakodon
dishes.description: Chicken and egg simmered together over rice; name means 'parent and child bowl'.
steps: Simmer sliced onion in dashi, soy sauce, and mirin until softened.
Add sliced chicken and cook until nearly done.
Pour beaten eggs evenly over the top and cover.
Cook just until the eggs are softly set, not fully firm.
Slide the whole mixture over a bowl of hot rice to serve.

dishes.name: Samgyeopsal
dishes.description: Thick-cut pork belly grilled at the table and wrapped in lettuce.
steps: Heat a grill or heavy pan until very hot.
Grill the thick pork belly slices, turning occasionally, until crisp outside and cooked through.
Grill sliced garlic alongside for a few minutes.
Snip the cooked pork into bite-sized pieces with kitchen scissors.
Wrap pieces in lettuce with garlic and a dab of ssamjang to eat.

dishes.name: Sundubu Jjigae
dishes.description: Bubbling, spicy soft tofu stew served in a stone pot.
steps: Sauté pork or seafood with gochugaru in a little oil until fragrant.
Add water or stock and bring to a simmer.
Spoon in the soft tofu in large chunks without stirring too much.
Simmer until everything is cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Crack an egg into the center just before serving, letting the residual heat cook it.

dishes.name: Sichuan Hot Pot
dishes.description: Communal simmering pot of fiery, numbing broth for cooking meat and vegetables tableside.
steps: Bring the prepared hot pot broth to a simmer in a pot at the center of the table.
Arrange thinly sliced meats and vegetables on platters around the pot.
Each diner cooks their own ingredients briefly in the simmering broth using chopsticks or a strainer.
Dip cooked items in the sesame-garlic sauce before eating.
Continue adding ingredients to the pot throughout the meal.

dishes.name: Xinjiang Lamb Skewers
dishes.description: Cumin-and-chili-crusted grilled lamb skewers from China's Xinjiang region.
steps: Thread cubed lamb onto skewers, leaving a little fat for flavor.
Mix cumin, chili flakes, and salt together.
Grill the skewers over high heat, turning frequently.
Sprinkle the spice mixture generously over the skewers while they cook.
Serve hot, straight off the grill.

dishes.name: Cantonese Roast Goose
dishes.description: Crackling-skinned roast goose, a Cantonese specialty.
steps: Season the goose cavity generously with five-spice.
Blanch the skin briefly with boiling water, then air-dry uncovered in the fridge for several hours.
Brush the skin with a glaze of maltose, vinegar, and soy sauce.
Roast at high heat, turning as needed, until the skin is deep mahogany and crackling.
Rest before carving into thin slices.

dishes.name: Macher Jhol
dishes.description: Bengali light fish curry, a staple of everyday Bengali meals.
steps: Rub fish steaks with turmeric and a little salt, then lightly fry in mustard oil until golden, and set aside.
In the same oil, fry potato cubes until lightly browned.
Add tomato and a light spice blend, cooking until it forms a thin sauce.
Add water and bring to a simmer, then return the fish to the pan.
Simmer gently until the fish is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.

dishes.name: Litti Chokha
dishes.description: Bihar's rustic dish of roasted stuffed wheat balls with mashed vegetables.
steps: Make a stiff wheat dough and rest it.
Mix sattu with mustard oil, spices, and a little water to make the filling.
Stuff dough balls with the sattu filling and seal well.
Roast over an open flame or bake until the crust is browned and slightly cracked.
Mash roasted eggplant and potato with mustard oil and spices, and serve alongside.

dishes.name: Sarson ka Saag
dishes.description: Punjabi mustard greens curry, classically paired with cornbread.
steps: Simmer mustard greens and spinach in a little water until very soft.
Blend the cooked greens with ginger into a coarse puree.
Return to the pot and stir in cornmeal to thicken slightly.
Simmer another 10 minutes, stirring often.
Finish with a generous knob of butter and serve with makki di roti.

dishes.name: Rasam
dishes.description: Thin, peppery South Indian soup often eaten with rice.
steps: Simmer tamarind pulp with water and chopped tomato for 10 minutes.
Add crushed black pepper and a pinch of turmeric.
Temper cumin seeds and curry leaves in hot oil, then add to the pot.
Simmer another 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Serve hot, often poured over rice.

dishes.name: Payasam
dishes.description: South Indian sweet milk pudding, served at festivals.
steps: Toast vermicelli or rice lightly in a little ghee.
Add milk and simmer until the vermicelli or rice is fully cooked and the milk has thickened.
Stir in jaggery or sugar until dissolved.
Add cardamom for fragrance.
Fry cashews and raisins in ghee and stir in just before serving, warm or chilled.

dishes.name: Bánh Xèo
dishes.description: Crispy Vietnamese savory crepe folded around shrimp and pork.
steps: Mix rice flour batter with turmeric for color.
Sauté shrimp and pork in a hot pan, then pour in a thin layer of batter.
Add bean sprouts on one half of the crepe.
Cook until the edges are crisp and lacy, then fold in half like an omelet.
Serve with lettuce and herbs for wrapping, plus a dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Cao Lầu
dishes.description: Regional Vietnamese noodle dish unique to the town of Hoi An.
steps: Prepare thick, chewy rice noodles (traditionally made with a specific local water).
Braise or roast pork until tender and flavorful, then slice thinly.
Toss the noodles with a small amount of the pork braising liquid.
Top with sliced pork, fresh greens, and crispy fried noodle croutons.
Serve with just a small amount of broth, unlike a full noodle soup.

dishes.name: Mango Sticky Rice
dishes.description: Sweet coconut sticky rice served with ripe mango slices.
steps: Soak glutinous rice for several hours, then steam until tender and translucent.
Warm coconut milk with sugar and a pinch of salt until dissolved.
Pour most of the coconut mixture over the hot steamed rice and let it absorb.
Slice ripe mango.
Serve the rice alongside mango slices, drizzled with the remaining coconut sauce.

dishes.name: Tom Kha Gai
dishes.description: Creamy, tangy coconut chicken soup, milder than tom yum.
steps: Simmer coconut milk with galangal and lemongrass to infuse the flavors.
Add sliced chicken and cook until just done.
Season with fish sauce and a little sugar.
Remove from heat and stir in lime juice.
Garnish with cilantro and sliced chili before serving.

dishes.name: Soto Ayam
dishes.description: Indonesian turmeric-spiced chicken soup.
steps: Simmer chicken with turmeric, lemongrass, and aromatics until tender.
Remove chicken, shred it, and strain the broth.
Cook vermicelli separately.
Assemble bowls with vermicelli, shredded chicken, and sliced boiled egg.
Ladle the hot turmeric broth over the top and garnish with fried shallots.

dishes.name: Rawon
dishes.description: Dark, earthy East Javanese beef stew colored by black nuts.
steps: Brown beef cubes with onion and aromatics.
Stir in black keluak paste, giving the dish its distinctive dark color.
Add tamarind and enough water to cover, then simmer until the beef is tender, about 1.5 hours.
Season to balance the earthy, tangy flavor.
Serve with rice and fresh bean sprouts on top.

dishes.name: Bicol Express
dishes.description: Spicy Filipino pork stew named after a train route, cooked in coconut milk.
steps: Sauté garlic and chili until fragrant.
Add sliced pork belly and brown lightly.
Add coconut milk and shrimp paste, bringing to a simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and thickens, about 30-40 minutes.
Serve hot with rice.

dishes.name: Tapsilog
dishes.description: Filipino breakfast combo of cured beef, fried rice, and egg.
steps: Pan-fry the cured beef until browned and cooked through.
Fry rice with minced garlic until fragrant and slightly crisp.
Fry eggs sunny-side up.
Plate the beef, garlic rice, and egg together.
Serve with a small bowl of vinegar-garlic dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Baba Ganoush
dishes.description: Smoky roasted eggplant dip, a Levantine mezze staple.
steps: Roast whole eggplants over an open flame or in a hot oven until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft.
Let cool, then peel and scoop out the flesh.
Blend or mash the flesh with tahini, garlic, and lemon juice.
Season with salt and a little cumin.
Drizzle with olive oil before serving.

dishes.name: Manakish
dishes.description: Lebanese flatbread topped with za'atar and olive oil, eaten for breakfast.
steps: Mix za'atar with enough olive oil to form a spreadable paste.
Roll dough into rounds.
Spread the za'atar mixture generously over each round.
Bake at high heat until the edges are golden and crisp, about 8-10 minutes.
Serve warm, often folded in half.

dishes.name: Knafeh
dishes.description: Warm, syrup-soaked cheese pastry topped with crushed pistachios.
steps: Toss shredded phyllo with melted butter until evenly coated.
Press half the phyllo into a round pan.
Spread the sweet cheese evenly over the phyllo layer.
Top with the remaining phyllo, pressing down firmly.
Bake until golden, then immediately soak with sugar syrup and top with crushed pistachios.

dishes.name: Falooda
dishes.description: Layered rose-flavored milk dessert with vermicelli and basil seeds.
steps: Cook thin vermicelli noodles until soft, then cool.
Layer rose syrup at the bottom of a tall glass.
Add soaked basil seeds and cooked noodles on top.
Pour chilled milk over the layers.
Top with a scoop of ice cream and a drizzle of extra rose syrup.

dishes.name: Pounded Yam
dishes.description: Smooth, stretchy staple made by pounding boiled yam, eaten with soup.
steps: Boil peeled yam chunks in water until very soft, about 20-25 minutes.
Drain well.
Pound the hot yam in a mortar (or use a stand mixer with a dough hook) until completely smooth and stretchy.
Wet hands or tools periodically to prevent sticking.
Shape into a smooth mound and serve with soup.

dishes.name: Red Red
dishes.description: Ghanaian bean stew named for its red palm oil color, served with fried plantain.
steps: Cook black-eyed peas until tender, about 45 minutes.
Sauté onion in palm oil until soft, then add tomato paste and cook until fragrant.
Combine the cooked beans with the tomato-onion base and simmer 10 minutes.
Fry sliced ripe plantain until caramelized.
Serve the beans with the fried plantain on the side.

dishes.name: Canjeero
dishes.description: Somali spongy fermented flatbread, similar in spirit to injera.
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, and sugar into a thin batter.
Let it ferment at room temperature for several hours until bubbly.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan.
Pour a ladle of batter and swirl or spread thin, covering and cooking until the top is set and small holes form.
Serve warm, often with honey or stew.

dishes.name: Bariis Iskukaris
dishes.description: Somali spiced rice dish, often served at gatherings.
steps: Brown meat with onion and xawaash spice blend.
Add water or stock and simmer until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, reserving the spiced broth.
Cook rice in the reserved broth until tender and fragrant.
Combine rice and meat, topping with raisins before serving.

dishes.name: Cepelinai
dishes.description: Zeppelin-shaped Lithuanian potato dumplings stuffed with meat.
steps: Grate raw potato and squeeze out excess liquid, reserving the starch that settles.
Mix the grated potato with mashed potato and reserved starch to form a dough.
Mix ground pork with minced onion for the filling.
Shape dough around a portion of filling into a large oval (zeppelin shape).
